caption: Figure 5. Illustration of the PagedAttention algorithm, where the attention key and values vectors are stored as non-contiguous blocks in the memory.
subject: how one query token's key/value vectors are spread across three fixed-size blocks stored non-contiguously in physical memory

groups.why_chosen: One request's key/value vectors are split into fixed-size blocks (4 tokens each) that PagedAttention stores in whatever physical block-table slots are free, so logically adjacent blocks need not be physically contiguous.
groups.what_to_learn: Draw the container bigger than the data when the *absence* is the point; fan-out arrows to the occupied rows only
